title: Playback event consumer with manual acks
name: Playback event consumer

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this consumer guarantees that every playback event is eventually applied? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The container crashes after watchHistory.apply(event) succeeds but before ack.acknowledge() commits the offset. What happens when the partition is reassigned?
choices: The event is lost, because its offset was never committed.
The event is redelivered, markIfNew returns false, and the listener acks without applying it a second time.
The event is redelivered and applied again, incrementing completions twice.
The record is sent straight to the dead-letter topic because the previous attempt did not finish.

questions.prompt: In WatchHistoryRepository.apply, why is position_seconds written with GREATEST(...)?
choices: To make the SQL portable between databases.
To make completions idempotent, so a replayed COMPLETED event cannot double count.
To keep the stored position from moving backwards when events are redelivered or reordered, so replays of older progress events are harmless for that column.
To resolve write conflicts between the three consumer threads by serialising them.

questions.prompt: A malformed event makes watchHistory.apply throw an exception on every attempt. With the configured error handler, what is the outcome for that record?
choices: The listener thread retries it forever, blocking the partition.
The record is dropped after the first failure and the offset is committed.
The partition is paused until an operator fixes the data.
It is retried with exponential backoff for up to about 15 seconds, then published to the dead-letter topic and the consumer moves past it.
